about_the_game:
Song of Morus: Limbo Express is a third person shooter game inspired by Hong Kong folklores. In this game, you will control a young taoist priestess named Wong Chung Song (or her friends) and help the deity of Death to escort his underworld train.It will be a total bizarre combat experience as you spider-walk on a speeding train while shooting enemies, dodging obstacles, and bullet-hell .. in hells.

Motion Transcendence

I believe you can handle it. Most of the action games send effort to avoid motion sickness in hope of serving the majorities. In other words, they never offer the excitment that you probably can handle and enjoy. My game will guide you to skim the edge of motion transcendence, with bite-sized game levels and calm learning curve. Don't be afraid; only try.

Inspirations

The protagonists are based on Hong Kong Jiangshi movie fiction, and the idea of a spirtual train, is based on Hong Kong urban legend. We have ghost stories about non-existent subway stations for ghost. The game also includes lots of other local culture elements, that you can read after beating a level.

GamePlay

Jump out of the train and walk on the curve of exterior. You will have to control your character to defeat the enemies. Each player characters have their own abilities for
1. Melee Attack
2. Range Attack
3. Dash Attack
The difficult part is mastering spatial awareness. Here is some hints:
1. Use your peripheral vision—track threats at the edge of your screen.
2. Keep moving—it enhances your depth perception.
3. The train itself is your cover—use its shape to your advantage.

content_descriptors.notes:
* Religious Themes Disclaimer
This game is inspired by local folklore and religious elements; however, it is a work of fiction and diverges significantly from traditional beliefs. It is created purely for entertainment purposes and is not intended as an educational or religious representation.

* Depiction of Hell
The game features fictional depictions of various interpretations of hell. These portrayals are stylized and toned down for a broader audience, and may not align with the beliefs or expectations of all players.
